newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels kill two police, injure civilians.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels kill two police, injure civilians.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed two policemen and injured three civilians in a grenade and bomb attack on a police post in the northeast Colombian city of Cucuta, the authorities said on Sunday.

The building, in a middle-class residential district of the city, was partly destroyed in the raid, which police said was carried out by militias of the National Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest guerrilla force, on Saturday night.
A police spokesman said he did not know how many ELN rebels took part in the attack.

In the southern Colombian province of Caqueta, meanwhile, hopes faded that the country's largest guerrilla army, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), would release the 60 soldiers they took prisoner more than three months ago.

The government's 10-day demilitarization period of a 5,400 square mile (14,000 sq km) swathe of jungle was due to expire at midnight Monday. The FARC's demands for further concessions to permit its safe access in and out of the handover zone have been rejected by the military and the government.

But the NTC TV news programme reported on Sunday that mothers of two of the soldiers, seized when the FARC overran a military base on Aug. 30, had been contacted by the guerrilla leadership in the province, who assured them all the captives were alive and in good health.
